doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Paul Desmond and having your own sound
summary: Rowe recalls hearing Brubeck at Eastman; Caputo praises Desmond and urges students to find their own sound.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I heard them, in oh gosh it must have been probably around ‘65 I think. Would that make sense? They were together then right? At the Eastman School of Music. And that was a good one. But I just remember how unassuming Desmond especially. You know I mean he looked like a banker or something. But he had that sense of, if you could sit down and write out a perfect solo, he already played it.

Yeah definitely a lyricist, a wonderful, wonderful player. Something about Paul Desmond to this day you can hear a saxophone and you know right away. Something that you don’t hear from the younger players today. Everybody is tending to sound the same. When you hear Phil Woods you know it’s Phil Woods. Paul Desmond, you know it’s him. Joe Morello you know it’s him. Tony. Drummers tend, and other musicians too tend to want to sound all alike. You know it’s probably the fault of sound men, they have one sound, there’s one drum sound, there’s one saxophone sound, but it shouldn’t be that way. Everybody should strive for their own sound and their own style. And that’s something that I try and talk to my students about, don’t sound like me, please. Don’t buy Buddy Rich videos and try and sound exactly like him. You know, imitate, assimilate, innovate.
